content.text: Durak ('Fool' in Russian) is Russia's most widely played card game. The goal is to NOT be the last player holding cardsâ€”the last player is the 'Durak' (Fool). Players attack with cards; the defender must beat each attacking card with a higher card of the same suit or any trump. If unable to defend, they take all attacked cards into their hand. A 36-card deck is used (6 through Ace). After each bout, players draw to replenish to 6 cards. The Podkidnoy (passing) variantâ€”where the attack can be redirected to the next playerâ€”is the standard form.

One of Russia's oldest documented card games. References appear from at least the 18th century. It was the default family card game across the Soviet Union and remains the most ubiquitous Russian card game today.

Two to six players. Best with four playing in partnerships (two against two, partners opposite). Can also be played by two to six as individuals, or six in two teams of three sitting alternately. The player to the dealer's left is the first defender; the attacker sits to the defender's right.
36 cards: Ranks 6-7-8-9-10-J-Q-K-A in each of 4 suits.
6 cards each. Turn one card as trump indicator; place under stock (suit visible). Stock face-down on top.

items.text: Prostoy Durak (Simple): No passing. Defender must simply beat all attacks or take. Simpler variant.
Perevodnoy Durak (Transfer): Defender can always pass the attack to next player if they have a matching cardâ€”even after defending a card.
Cooperative Durak: All players except the defender cooperate to attack together.
